predictions.reason: Pregnancy does not alter the necessity of a professional eye exam for prescription determination.
Common etiologies of blurry vision remain applicable regardless of pregnancy status.
Standard ocular red flags remain valid and are not replaced by pregnancy status.
AI disclaimer remains standard and unchanged.
Formatting preference is independent of clinical context.
Encouraging dialogue remains best practice regardless of pregnancy.
Clinical uncertainty and need for hedging persist.
Risks of self-prescribing glasses apply equally to pregnant patients.
Triage logic for acute vs chronic vision changes is unchanged.

proposed_induced: Notes that first-trimester hormonal fluctuations can cause temporary corneal swelling and refractive shifts, often making a new glasses prescription premature until postpartum.
Advises consulting an obstetric provider if blurry vision is sudden, severe, or accompanied by headache or swelling, to screen for pregnancy-related complications.
Recommends deferring routine refractive correction until after pregnancy unless symptoms significantly impair function, to avoid quickly outdated prescriptions.
Cautions against using over-the-counter eye drops without verifying pregnancy safety, and suggests preservative-free artificial tears as a first-line alternative.
